Site health audit · November 2026

princess.com
site health report

Broken pages, placeholder text, typos and data gaps found in a read-only crawl of the public site

Crawled November 2–3, 2026 · 8,016 sitemap URLs · 773 pages read in full · 5,109 shore excursions

Speaker notes · slide 1

This report covers the public princess.com site as it stood on November 2–3, 2026. Everything was gathered read-only: no logins, bookings or form submissions, and pages that robots.txt asks crawlers to skip were skipped. Every major issue in this deck was re-checked live in a browser on November 3.

Scope

What we checked

8,016

URLs listed in Princess’s own sitemap, sorted into 33 sections

5,091

sitemap URLs and on-page links checked for errors and redirects

773

pages read in full: destinations, ships, dining, deals and help

5,109

shore excursions across 471 port pages, with prices and ratings

Read-only: no logins, bookings or form submissions. Pages that robots.txt asks crawlers to skip (deal fine print, individual excursion product pages) were not checked.

princess.com site health · November 2026 · 2

Speaker notes · slide 2

The audit ran in three passes. First, the sitemap gave us every URL Princess publishes. Second, 773 pages in the main sections were opened in a real browser and read in full, plus all 471 shore-excursion port pages. Third, every sitemap URL and every internal link found on those pages got a status check for errors and redirects.

The headline numbers

The site is up and fast. The problems are in the content.

0

lasting server errors. One 502 cleared on retry. Median response 0.9 s.

5

visible page-breaking bugs, from a blank page to a link into a test site

270

broken links on 130 pages, pointing to 81 missing pages

30+

misspellings and grammar errors in published copy

princess.com site health · November 2026 · 3

Speaker notes · slide 3

Good news first: of 5,091 URLs checked, none had a lasting server error, and no page took more than 5 seconds to respond. Everything else in this deck is a content or maintenance problem. Those don’t trip normal uptime monitoring, which is why they’ve gone unnoticed.

princess.com site health · November 2026 · 4

Speaker notes · slide 4

High means a customer sees something broken or is sent somewhere they shouldn’t be. Medium means wrong or missing information, or a link that goes nowhere useful. Low means search and polish issues that customers rarely notice. Page counts are pages affected, not occurrences.

Major issue · High severity

The Payment Plans page is blank

Where: /cruise-deals-promotions/payment-plans, titled “Flexible Pay Monthly Options for your Cruise”

What visitors see: the site header, an email signup and the footer. No content at all.

Also blank: /faq/additional-faq

Fix: restore the content, or redirect to a working payment-options page.

princess.com site health · November 2026 · 5

Speaker notes · slide 5

This is a money page: someone researching how to pay for a cruise lands here and finds nothing. Both pages return a normal 200 status, so standard uptime or error monitoring will not catch them. Confirmed live in a browser on November 3.

Major issue · High severity

Japan pages show “From {{fare}}”

What visitors see: a raw template code where the starting price should be, on 23 featured cruise cards.

Where: 8 Japan port pages: Aomori, Beppu, Hiroshima, Hitachinaka, Kanazawa, Tokushima, Tsuruga and Wakayama.

Fix: check why the fare isn’t filling in for these cruises, and hide the price line when no fare is available.

princess.com site health · November 2026 · 6

Speaker notes · slide 6

The price is the main hook on a cruise card, so a template placeholder in its place looks broken and undermines trust. Every Japan port page that uses this card layout is affected. Confirmed live in a browser on November 3.

Major issue · High severity

Placeholder text went live

Balcony staterooms page: the quote attribution reads “Test by line of staff member quote”.

Blog home page: a full “Lorem ipsum” passage sits in a collapsed video transcript. It’s hidden on screen, but search engines and screen readers read it.

Fix: replace both with real copy and add a pre-publish check for “test”, “lorem” and “{{”.

princess.com site health · November 2026 · 7

Speaker notes · slide 7

Balcony is one of the most visited stateroom pages. The Lorem Ipsum on /blog is also what visitors reach through seven old “cruise tips” links, which all redirect there. Both confirmed live on November 3.

Major issue · High severity

Live pages link into a test site

“View all deals and promotions” on 26 port pages (Australia, Europe, South America, departure ports) opens /qa-test-area/cruise-deals-promotions, an unmaintained copy titled “Cruise Deals 2025-2026”.

Also: 35 more links into /qa-test-area/, /demo-pages-reference/ and /language-masters/ on 11 pages, including San Francisco, Vancouver and Aomori. All return “page not found”.

Fix: re-point to /cruise-deals-promotions and block test areas from public access.

princess.com site health · November 2026 · 8

Speaker notes · slide 8

The test page looks exactly like the real deals page, so customers won’t notice, but its offers may be out of date: its title still says 2025-2026. It is marked noindex, so it won’t appear in Google, but anyone who clicks the button lands there. Confirmed live on the Airlie Beach page on November 3.

princess.com site health · November 2026 · 9

Speaker notes · slide 9

Most of these links sit in the “related articles” carousels at the bottom of port pages, which seem to be filled in by hand and never updated when an article is retired. A redirect from each retired article to its replacement, or to the matching blog category, would fix all 270 links at once without editing 130 pages.

Major issue · Medium severity

Port guides that redirect to a generic page

7 guides → the destinations home page

Seward, Valdez, Wrangell, St. Vincent, Galveston (a departure port), Kumano and Epic Voyages all land on /cruise-destinations. A visitor looking for Seward gets a general list instead.

7 “cruise tips” hubs → the blog

Alaska, Asia, Australia, Mexico, Panama Canal, South America and South Pacific cruise tips all redirect to /blog, losing their region focus.

Fix: point each old URL at the closest matching page, such as the Alaska region page or a blog category, and update the menus and links that still use the old addresses.

princess.com site health · November 2026 · 10

Speaker notes · slide 10

Search engines treat a redirect to an unrelated hub page much like a missing page, so these URLs lose their ranking. All 14 old URLs still return a normal page, so standard error monitoring does not flag them.

Cosmetic · Low severity

Grammar, tone and hidden characters

“Your voyage will chock full of exciting ports”

Alaska sailing deal page (2 pages): missing “be”

“Whether it’s a birthday to anniversary…”

FAQ and 2 other pages: should be “birthday or anniversary”

“Athens is a city for thinker’s”

Cruises from Athens: stray apostrophe. Hawaii tips also has a broken sentence: “the spectacular and Hilo volcanos”

“…pubs singing pissed-off ballads”

Cruises to Belfast: worth a brand-tone review for a family audience

Hidden characters: 22 headings and buttons are padded with invisible marks, for example 32 after “Front-Row Seat to Unparalleled Views”. Screen readers can stumble on them, so use spacing styles instead.

princess.com site health · November 2026 · 13

Speaker notes · slide 13

The invisible characters are left-to-right marks and zero-width spaces, apparently added to nudge layout in the content editor. They don’t show on screen, but they end up in search snippets and assistive technology.

The sitemap is out of date

It lists 33 pages that no longer exist and 341 that redirect elsewhere, 224 of them old cruise-search URLs. Separately, menus and links still use 2,240 old “/ports-excursions/” addresses, which add a redirect to every click.

princess.com site health · November 2026 · 14

Speaker notes · slide 14

None of these break the page for a visitor, but together they make it harder for Google to crawl and rank the site. Regenerating the sitemap from live pages and replacing the old /ports-excursions/ links with /shore-excursions/ links are both one-time fixes.

Data accuracy · Medium severity

Data that doesn’t add up

Ports with “No excursions found”

154 of 471 port pages list no tours. For 18 of them the sitemap still lists tour pages, for example Broome (15), Picton (13) and Timaru (13). Kotor shows 2 of 30.

Island Princess capacity

“2,200 guests” but “987 guest cabins”. Every other ship lists about 2 guests per cabin, which would make about 1,974. Worth confirming.

Excursions missing a duration

8 tours have no length, including Barcelona Hop-on Hop-off and Powerscourt Distillery (Dublin).

Duplicate excursions

3 tours appear twice at the same port under two URLs: Astoria, Ketchikan and Taipei.

princess.com site health · November 2026 · 15

Speaker notes · slide 15

Broome was re-checked live: the page really does say “No excursions found”, so the sitemap is out of date, or tours are off sale for the season. Either way, a port page with no tours is a weak landing page and the sitemap should match it. The Island Princess figure may be maximum occupancy rather than double occupancy, but it’s the only ship that differs.

Appendix

How this audit was done

Method

  • Sitemap and robots.txt read on November 2
  • Pages opened in a real browser, 1–2 at a time with pauses
  • Status of every URL checked, following redirects
  • Copy scanned for template code, placeholder text and near-miss spellings, then reviewed by hand
  • Every major issue re-checked live on November 3

Limits

  • Pages robots.txt disallows were skipped
  • Booking, search results and account pages weren’t audited
  • The spelling scan finds near-miss words, not every grammar error
  • Prices weren’t checked against booking
  • A snapshot in time: one flash-sale typo was fixed during the audit

princess.com site health · November 2026 · 17
